text.p: Botswana's Finance Minister Festus Mogae announced on Monday several measures to tackle rising unemployment, especially in the manufacturing sector.
"Our priority as a nation for the years to come should be to continue to increase employment opportunities and enhance productivity," Mogae said in his 1997/98 budget speech to the national assembly.
The budget is expected to result in a 763 million pula surplus and increase government cash balances by 802 million pula.
Official statistics show Botswana's unemployment at 30 percent, but some economists believe unemployment could be as high as 50 percent if the informal sector was excluded.
Mogae said formal sector employment grew marginally by 0.8 percent annually to March 1996, but stressed that this was not enough.
"This marginal growth in formal employment is a cause for concern and continues to pose a major challenge to policy-makers," he told the national assembly.

"The most effective way to minimise unemployment is to maintain high rates of economic growth. This implies a need for significant foreign investment, which necessitates an adequate skill base to accommodate the investment.
"Government is in the process of expanding the system of vocational and technical education and of reorienting instructional methods in favour of competency-based techniques."
To stimulate local manufacture, Mogae announced the introduction of a Local Procurement Programme with effect from April 1997.
"We will channel a proportion of central government's supplies procurement to local manufacturers," he said.

To qualify, companies will have to employ not more than 200 people, have an annual turnover of between 200,000 pula and five million pula, and have an investment in productive machinery of between 50,000 pula and five million pula.
The programme will be operated on a pilot basis for three years, Mogae said.
Additionally, the Productive Employment Development Fund, which gives assistance to small businesses, will be increased to 72 million pula from 40 million pula last year.
Via his own ministry, Mogae has allocated 72 million pula for the Botswana Development Corporation to build factory shells and 10 million pula for the Botswana Technology Centre.
He also announced 40 million pula for improved vocational training facilities and 30 million pula for the University of Botswana.
